title: Crispi Smashed Potatoes with Malt Vinegar and Dill Gravy
description: Peeled baby potatoes braise in the Crispi and are gently smashed into a warm dill gravy with a little malt vinegar.
equipment: Ninja Crispi PowerPod with US Bake preset and 6-cup glass container

ingredients.name: baby yellow potatoes
ingredients.note: Peel and cut to pieces 1/2 inch thick.

ingredients.name: low-sodium mushroom broth
ingredients.note: Choose plain broth made with mushrooms and water.

ingredients.name: fresh dill fronds
ingredients.note: Mince finely and leave out coarse stems.

steps.title: Set up the Crispi
steps.text: Use the room-temperature 6-cup Ninja glass container without its crisper plate or an adapter. Leave off the storage lid. Load the container before starting the PowerPod.

steps.title: Load the potatoes
steps.text: Arrange {potatoes} and {broth} in the unheated glass. Settle the pieces in an even layer with as many cut faces as possible against the liquid.

steps.title: Braise on Bake
steps.text: Seat the PowerPod and select Bake. Turn the pieces through the liquid after 10 minutes with a silicone spoon. Cook for another 8–18 minutes, until even the largest piece flattens under a fork.

steps.title: Smash in the serving bowls
steps.text: Lift the potatoes into warm bowls and crush each piece gently in a spoonful of the cooking liquid. Leave the bowls loosely covered.

steps.title: Warm the dill base
steps.text: Ladle the remaining potato liquid into the HexClad and bring to a simmer. Stir in {dill} for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Bring the base to a simmer. Whisk in the freshly stirred slurry and let it bubble for 1 minute, stirring until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Finish with malt vinegar
steps.text: Stir {vinegar} and {butter} into the gravy off heat. Spoon it generously into the broken potato centers.

notes: Make ahead: Cut the potatoes the day before and refrigerate submerged in clean water; drain before cooking. Refrigerate leftovers for up to 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: No. These lightly smashed pieces can turn grainy after freezing. The dill gravy can be frozen separately for up to 1 month. Fridge reheat: Warm a single portion, covered, in the HexClad with a splash of broth or water. Stir or turn gently and heat to 165°F throughout. Freezer reheat: If already frozen, thaw in the refrigerator overnight and warm covered in gravy to 165°F. Mash more thoroughly if the texture is grainy. Option A uses malt vinegar. For gentler Option B, omit it and use a little extra dill. For dairy-free potatoes omit the finishing butter. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/2 of recipe): 145 kcal, 3.5 g protein, 28.6 g total carbohydrate, 2.1 g fat, 1.9 g fiber, 16 mg sodium. Includes the measured broth and sauce. Sodium varies with your broth.
